title: XOR After Range Multiplication Queries II
summary: Given an integer array nums and a 2D integer array queries where each query is represented as [li, ri, ki, vi], perform the following operations for each query: 1.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a 2D integer array queries where each query is represented as [li, ri, ki, vi], perform the following operations for each query: 1. Initialize idx to li. 2. While idx is less than or equal to ri: - Update nums[idx] to (nums[idx] * vi) % (10^9 + 7). - Increment idx by ki. 3. After processing all queries, return the bitwise XOR of all elements in nums.
constraints: Each inclusive arithmetic-progression range is multiplied modulo 1,000,000,007.
Return the XOR after all queries.
hints: Large steps touch few indices; small steps share residue-class progressions that support multiplicative difference events.
Apply large-step queries directly and record start/inverse-end events for each small step and residue.
Sweep every small progression, maintaining its active multiplier modulo M, then XOR the final values.
A factor enters exactly at its first progression coordinate and its inverse removes it just after the last, so every query affects precisely its requested indices.
